items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The first night I played with Broadus was for a dance in Dayton, Ohio.

ctx.x: but being 21, it was more of a fancy to have a girl friend or a lover.

Not long after this romance started, a band leader by the name of Broadus from Lexington, Ky, asked me if I would join him for a month and I told Page that I would like to leave for a change of places. So I accepted the offer of Broadus. Broadus had been quite a big name in jazz and had played many Fraternity dances at Yale, Harvard and the college of Lexington among others. Love did not have such a hold on me that I did not want to travel even if it was not far.

The first night I played with Broadus was for a dance in Dayton, Ohio. Broadus and his musicians had come to Cincinnati early that morning and as I was not ready to leave with them, he told me that I could come to Dayton later by train. Dayton is about 50 miles from Cincinnati. Broadus travelled by car as did most of the orchestra then and today.
